items.title: Medical Image Segmentation: Foundation Model Adaptation versus Task-Specific Training
items.summary: The article examines whether foundation models pretrained on natural images can outperform task-specific models for medical image segmentation, noting limited evidence from biased comparisons.
items.whyItMatters: Tech-savvy readers should know foundation models may not yet reliably replace specialized training in medical imaging.

items.title: Toward Foundation Detection Models via Example-Based Grounding in EM-DETR
items.summary: The article discusses using example-based grounding in EM-DETR to build foundation detection models for medical lesion detection, addressing data scarcity and dataset heterogeneity.
items.whyItMatters: It could improve diagnostic AI accuracy with fewer annotations, benefiting clinicians and patients.

items.title: TorchCurves: Differentiable Parametric Curves
items.summary: TorchCurves is a PyTorch library that treats vector-valued parametric curves as learnable primitives, enabling differentiable mapping and joint optimization of curve coefficients.
items.whyItMatters: It lets tech-savvy developers embed trainable curves directly into neural networks for advanced shape modeling and graphics tasks.

items.title: AutoScaffold: AI-Guided Scaffolding for Reinforcement Learning of Language Models
items.summary: AutoScaffold uses AI to generate training-time scaffolds that convert detailed reward signals into actionable guidance for language model reinforcement learning.
items.whyItMatters: It automates scaffold design, improving learning efficiency and reducing human effort in RL for language models.

items.title: Contrastive Discovery: Open-Ended Scientific Discovery over Competing Explanations
items.summary: The paper introduces Contrastive Discovery, a method for LLM agents to evaluate competing scientific hypotheses, not just a single hypothesis versus its negation.
items.whyItMatters: It enables more accurate scientific inference, helping tech-savvy readers build better AI-driven research tools.

items.title: Pyrite: Building and Benchmarking Protein-Ligand Pose Ranking Agents
items.summary: Pyrite presents a benchmark of 1,500 protein‑ligand pose pairs to evaluate and improve pairwise pose‑ranking algorithms for drug discovery.
items.whyItMatters: It helps researchers assess and enhance ranking models, speeding up accurate ligand binding predictions for new therapeutics.

items.title: When Does the Real Wiring Win? Testing connectome structure-function claims against unmeasured physiology
items.summary: The article critiques connectome-constrained models, showing that improved performance may stem from parameter tuning rather than true wiring differences.
items.whyItMatters: It warns tech-savvy readers that claimed structure–function links might be artifacts of model fitting, not biological reality.

items.title: Continual-ARC: Measuring Skill Acquisition over a Working Lifetime
items.summary: The paper introduces Continual-ARC, a benchmark for measuring skill acquisition across a working lifetime, addressing limitations of existing continual learning tests.
items.whyItMatters: It enables fair comparison of memory- and weight-based systems, guiding AI research toward lifelong learning.

items.title: Emergent Biological Capabilities in a Foundation Model for Molecular Interactions
items.summary: Bonbon, a multimodal foundation model trained on 3.2 trillion protein‑ligand tokens, shows zero‑shot emergent capabilities for molecular interactions.
items.whyItMatters: It could accelerate drug discovery by predicting interactions without labeled data.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Agent Evaluation Frameworks: Stability, Detection, and Discovery in Enterprise Analytics Agents
items.summary: The article compares three evaluation frameworks for enterprise LLM analytics agents, focusing on stability, failure detection, and discovery across complex workflows.
items.whyItMatters: Tech leaders need reliable agent assessment to ensure robust, error-free analytics in multi-tool enterprise environments.

items.title: ReTrace: Distilling Tool-Using Agents into Planner-Free Workflows
items.summary: ReTrace transforms natural‑language SOPs and logged agent runs into reusable, code‑based workflows, eliminating per‑step LLM calls.
items.whyItMatters: Reduces latency and cost for scaling LLM‑driven automation.

items.title: TimeSeek: Multi-Task and Multi-Domain Pretraining for Generalized Time Series Analytics
items.summary: TimeSeek introduces a multi-task, multi-domain pretraining framework to improve time series models by better capturing complex patterns across domains.
items.whyItMatters: It offers more adaptable, efficient models for diverse time‑series applications, boosting performance and reducing reliance on large Transformers.

items.title: Re-Search: Dissecting LLM Ideation Through a Two-Player Questioning Game
items.summary: Research ideation is iterative: researchers refine their ideas step by step based on feedback. items.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Needs a Logic of Inference
items.summary: Neural networks are increasingly studied not merely as predictive systems, but as complex systems whose internal computations are themselves objects of scientific inquiry. items.title: Pterodactyl: Pushing the Limits of Efficient Automated Translation Evaluation
items.summary: In this paper, we present 1020 Group's submission to the WMT26 shared task on automated quality evaluation. Our system, Pterodactyl, was engineered specifically for subtasks 2 and 3, that is, segment-level quality score prediction and the detection of error-free segments. Pterodactyl is a highly customizable, ultra-low cost system optimized for binary classification in translation triage and data…

items.title: FERN: Cross-Benchmark Table Retrieval for Text-to-SQL with Frozen Retrievers and Learned Ranking
items.summary: Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs. items.title: C^2-Routing: Complementary Cropping and Compression for Efficient Vision-Language Inference
items.summary: Visual Question Answering (VQA) imposes substantial computational overhead on vision-language models (VLMs), motivating model-agnostic input reduction methods that can be readily applied across diverse VLMs, including in black-box settings. items.title: Bayesian inverse problems and epidemic-threshold uncertainty for a heterogeneous SIS reaction-diffusion model
items.summary: We study Bayesian inference of persistence from early observations of a heterogeneous susceptible--infected--susceptible (SIS) reaction--diffusion model with standard incidence. We show that the leading prevalence dynamics depend on the unknown coefficients only through the difference between the transmission and recovery rates and the infected diffusivity. items.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
items.summary: Policy optimization is central to language model post-training, yet principled guidance remains limited. We revisit its theoretical foundations to identify algorithms that learn near-optimal policies using total samples and gradient steps governed by the base model's response coverage, a measure of how readily it generates optimal responses. items.title: A Theory of Cross-Validation Variance
items.summary: Cross-validation estimates predictive performance by repeatedly splitting the data into training and validation sets, fitting the model on the first and evaluating it on the second.
